needs.title: Repeat a known number of times

brief_problem: The hottest days of the week

previous.title: Repeat a known number of times

runs.text: An array keeps many values of the same type under a single name, and each one is found by its position.
The problem
The kiosk writes down the highest temperature of each day of the week, from Monday to Sunday. It wants to know
which days were hotter than the week's average
How does a program work it out?
Try it
Solve it by hand with these highs: 20, 23, 19, 25, 22, 18 and 26.
The sum is 153 and the average is 21.86. Tuesday (23), Thursday (25), Friday (22) and Sunday (26) are above the average.
Look at the order: first you added everything to know the average, and then you looked at each day again. You had to remember the seven temperatures.
Understand

inputs.text: seven temperatures, one per day, from Monday to Sunday.

outputs.text: the names of the days hotter than the average, one per line.

relation.text: the average is the sum divided by 7; the days whose temperature is above it are shown.

examples.text: all seven days at 20 → no day is above the average.

runs.text: The second example is an edge case: if all days are the same, none is above the average, and the program has to say so.
Plan

entries.text: Read the seven temperatures and add them up to know the average.
Walk through the temperatures again and show the days above the average.

caption.text: Two passes are needed: the first computes the average; the second compares each day with it.

runs.text: First pass: the seven temperatures are walked through and gathered for the average.
Second pass: they are walked through again and the days above the average are marked.
With what you know so far, keeping seven temperatures takes seven boxes with seven names, and the second pass would be impossible to write with a loop.
The new tool
An
array
is a row of cells of the same type under a single name. Each cell is found by its position, which is its
index
. Indices start at 0: an array of 7 cells goes from 0 to 6.

runs.text: To walk through an array, a counted loop takes the index from the first cell to the last. That index has a role of its own:

description.text: An index that moves cell by cell, from the first to the last.

Test
Improve
In one sentence:
The program keeps the week's temperatures, computes the average and shows the days above it
Compare it with a version with seven loose boxes: if the week had 30 days, you would have to add 23 boxes, 23 reads and 23 comparisons. With arrays, changing the 7 and the 6 is enough.
What you learned

points.text: An array keeps values of the same type; the index is the position and it starts at 0.
A walker is the index that moves cell by cell.
Using an index that does not exist is an out of range error and stops the program.
